reason: A defect in scoring, found on 14 November 2026 from the website's Lab: the interim record showed 32 scored tournament-start forecasts and 59.4% favourites won (19/32), while the ledger table below it showed 31 scored and 19 favourites won. The difference is one match. ESPN reused its match number 187384 when a player was replaced at the WTA Finals: it was Andreeva v Muchova when the counted forecast was issued (12 November, 00:19Z) and Andreeva v Shnaider when it was played (13 November). Results are attached by provider match number, so the result of the match played (Andreeva beat Shnaider 6-2 6-1) was stored as the result of Andreeva v Muchova, and outcome_rows scored it, because the recorded winner is one of the forecast's two players. The website has checked the players itself since 10 November 2026 (web/publisher/views.py, Snapshot.replaced, written after ESPN 186526 changed from Van Assche v Shevchenko to Mannarino v Shevchenko; that match had no forecast) and shows such a match as not played, but the protocol's scoring did not.
fix: prospective.result_from_other_players traces each result row of a settlement to the provider record it came from (same provider and match number, the last record retrieved at or before the result) and compares that record's two provider player ids with the provider ids the forecast stored (inputs.players.a/b.provider_id). If they differ, outcome_rows excludes the forecast with the reason prospective.REPLACED ('players changed before the match (the result is from a replacement match)'), before the status check. Result rows from another provider, and forecasts or records without provider ids, are not judged, so nothing else changes. Regression tests: tests/test_forecast_prospective.py ReplacementMatchTests (test_a_result_from_a_replacement_match_is_not_scored fails on the previous code, which scores the match; the two other tests show that the same players and other providers are scored as before).
features_unchanged: Yes. Only the evaluation code changes (prospective.result_from_other_players and one exclusion in prospective.outcome_rows). Nothing on the inference path calls either: fixtures, history, features, the replay and the stored forecasts are untouched.
models_unchanged: Yes. models/phase4_tournament_start.json and models/phase4_round_aware_r0.json are unchanged (same artifact hashes).
eligibility_unchanged: Which fixtures are forecast and which forecast counts (the first stored, at least 30 minutes before the start, in the window) are unchanged. Which matches count is unchanged in intent: a counted forecast is scored on the result of the match it forecast; the code now enforces that when a provider reuses a match number, as it already did when a result names a player outside the forecast. Applied to the live store of 14 November 2026 (downloaded read-only), exactly one counted forecast is excluded (M-0f8b410e3a7468e2572f0ef0, tournament start, Muchova 50.1% v Andreeva) and no other forecast of either model.
outcomes_used: Yes, and disclosed. The defect was found from the published interim record, which shows results, and the result of the affected match was looked at to diagnose it. The rule does not depend on which way any result went: it is the player check the website has applied since 10 November 2026, written after the Van Assche case and before Andreeva v Shnaider was played, now applied to scoring. Its effect on the interim record of 14 November 2026: tournament start 32 to 31 scored matches, favourite won 19/32 (59.4%) to 19/31 (61.3%), log loss 0.6421 to 0.6403; round-aware unchanged (12 scored).
counting: forecasts carrying the previous fingerprint or this one count under the protocol's unchanged rules (first stored forecast, the same window, matches and metrics); stored forecasts are never changed. The amendment counts only once it is committed unchanged
